title: Canva releases its first image generation model
content:
Design platform Canva released its first image generation model, called Canva Craft, developed by its research team to compete with same-category models from Google, OpenAI, ByteDance, and Meta.
The company said its model works in two stages. In the first stage, it interprets users’ prompts and creates a plan with details like spatial relationships of elements, relative scale, visual hierarchy, and information for text generation. In the second stage, its model generates an image of up to 2K resolution in a possible 30 different aspect ratios for various platforms.
Canva said that this approach allows it to create images with accurate details of objects and legible text. Plus, users would be able to make precise edits without changing other parts of the image.
The company noted that rather than using photographs, it used designs to train this model using human-designed templates from Canva’s library, including posters, social posts, presentations, infographics, menus, and typography-rich layouts.
That means images generated with Canva Craft could be converted into layered designs using Canva Magic, the company’s image-to-design transformer. Last year, the platform released its own model that understands designs and layers.
Canva Craft is available on the company’s platform to all users, who can access the model from the Dream Lab tab. The model will also be available through the Canva API. Plus, the company plans to support image generation in third-party chatbots like ChatGPT and Gemini through Canva’s MCP.
Canva has used a bunch of image models for generation in its platform, so it’s likely that the new models will help save API costs for the company. It said that besides costs, the new model also allows the platform to have better quality and speed control.
In 2024, Canva acquired media generation platform Leonardo.ai. It said that the researchers from Leonardo contributed to the new image model.
Canva said that it is developing two cost-efficient versions of the model, called Craftfast and Craft-ultrafast, which will be released soon.
The company was on track for $4 billion in revenue last year. However, it cut its growth forecast for 2026, causing its valuation to reportedly plummet from $42 billion to $35 billion, according to external analysts.

report.summary: Canva launched Canva Craft, its first in-house image-generation model, trained on design templates to produce text-accurate, editable images and reduce reliance on external model APIs.
report.background: Canva built its business on making design tools accessible to non-professionals, but its AI image features have largely relied on third-party models. Releasing an in-house model puts Canva in direct competition with Google, OpenAI, ByteDance, and Meta, while giving it more control over quality, speed, and API costs. Canva acquired Leonardo.ai in 2024, and researchers from that team contributed to Craft. The launch also comes amid business pressure: Canva was reportedly on track for $4 billion in revenue, but it cut its 2026 growth forecast and analysts reportedly lowered its valuation from $42 billion to $35 billion. A proprietary model could help Canva differentiate its platform and improve margins as AI image generation becomes a standard design feature.
key_points: Canva Craft uses a two-stage process: first it interprets a prompt and plans spatial relationships, scale, visual hierarchy, and text placement; then it generates an image at up to 2K resolution in up to 30 aspect ratios. Canva says this produces accurate object details, legible text, and precise edits without altering unrelated parts of an image.

Unlike many image models trained on photographs, Craft was trained on human-designed Canva templates such as posters, social posts, presentations, infographics, menus, and typography-heavy layouts. This design-focused training is intended to make generated images more useful as editable design assets rather than standalone pictures.

Generated images can be converted into layered designs using Canva Magic, Canva's image-to-design transformer. That connection could let users move from AI-generated concept to editable template, combining generation with Canva's existing layer-aware design workflow.

Craft is available to all Canva users through the Dream Lab tab and through the Canva API. Canva also plans to support image generation in third-party chatbots like ChatGPT and Gemini through Canva's MCP, extending the model beyond Canva's own interface.

Canva expects Craft to reduce API costs and improve control over quality and speed. It is also developing two cheaper, faster versions called Craftfast and Craft-ultrafast, which will be released soon and could make high-volume generation more affordable.
report.impact: Canva Craft signals a shift from integrating third-party image models to building design-native generation in-house. For the AI industry, it shows that specialized training data—designs rather than photos—can be a differentiator, especially for legible text and editable layouts. For developers, Canva's API and MCP support create new integration paths, while lower-cost fast variants could make image generation cheaper at scale. For regular users, the bigger change is practical: generated images may arrive as layered, editable designs rather than flat pictures, fitting directly into workflows for social posts, presentations, and marketing materials. The competitive pressure on Google, OpenAI, and others is less about raw image quality and more about distribution inside everyday design tools.
report.tools: Watch Canva Craft in the Dream Lab tab, Canva Magic for converting images into layered designs, and Canva's API plus MCP connectors for ChatGPT and Gemini integrations. Leonardo.ai, acquired by Canva in 2024, remains relevant for media generation. For open-source experimentation, ComfyUI and Stable Diffusion-based workflows are useful for testing text rendering, layout control, and editing pipelines, though they are not direct substitutes for Canva's design-template training.
